passage: Four classmates each set out to learn the same new web tool in a fortnight. Naveen resisted opening the tutorials at first. He read what problem the tool was made to solve and what its main parts were, so every tutorial afterwards slotted into a map he already carried in his head. Rehana followed a short tutorial for a day, then started an expense tracker of her own. The errors that popped up taught her more than any video. Vinita signed up for course after course and nodded along at every lesson. But when she opened an empty file, she could not write a single line, and she realised that watching had felt like learning without building any skill. Tarun explained the idea to a junior from the lower year. At the second question he stumbled and saw a gap he had not known about. He went back, fixed that piece, and only then moved on to the next topic.

qa.q: What did Rehana build after her one-day tutorial?
How did Vinita's way of learning differ from Rehana's, and what result did each get?
qa.a: Vinita kept watching courses and could not write anything from an empty file. Rehana built a small project and learned from her errors, so she gained a working skill.

qa.q: What might Vinita be feeling when she stares at the empty file?
qa.a: She is likely frustrated and a bit ashamed, since all her hours of watching did not turn into something she can do.
She could pick a very small project and build it step by step, looking things up only when she is stuck. Explaining her progress to someone would show her what is still unclear. 🙂

grounding: Students learn a new technology by first grasping the core idea, building at once, only watching courses, and teaching back to find gaps.
